Release notes/v0.7.1/Oct 19, 2026

What's new in Cadence 0.7.1.

Cadence now aims higher when it picks work for your agents: bigger goals, its own ideas for long jobs toward them, and agents that keep going for hours until the job is done.

By Cadence Labs · Filed in Releases

§01 Changed

  • Goals aim higher. Each project's goal is now the outcome you could reach in about three months if your agents did most of the building, with a bar you can check ("25 people use it every day by January"). Goals Cadence drafted before redraft once on their own; goals you wrote stay as you wrote them.
  • Cadence's own ideas. Besides what you've said and tracked, Cadence reads each project's repo (what's missing, thin or unfinished) and proposes long jobs toward your goal, each a few hours of agent work, quoting the gap it rests on. They're marked Cadence's idea with about how many hours they take, start only on your yes, and turning one down never counts against Cadence's picks.
  • Agents keep going. A milestone agent ends each reply with where it stands. While there's more to do, Cadence tells it to keep going; when it needs you, its question waits in your Inbox; when it's done, its work is checked against your rules and waits for your tap. It stops when it's stuck (three turns without a new commit) or after ten hours, and its in-between turns don't fill your Inbox.
  • Run more at once. The day plan shows up to eight jobs and lets you choose how many run at once (three, unless you change it, up to six).
